standingInstructions.text: Operator rule for calls, in the operator's words: Don't name the high-rise buildings I've been avoiding (the Louise, the other high rises, the in-person pitches); naming them makes me less likely to do them. It has to feel more like a game.
standingInstructions.quote: And I'm not gonna do it at all because we're not approaching it correctly. We have to gamify it. And for you to get me to do that, you cannot mention the name of the high rises or else I will never do it.

operator.persona: Adam runs Laundry Farm, a small laundry pickup and delivery business in Los Angeles. He is creative and quick, and he resists work he dreads: he has not done any in-person pitching to apartment high-rises for about 80 days, and hearing the building names makes him want to avoid it more. He talks casually, in run-on spoken sentences, and gets irritated when the assistant talks more than he does or lists things at him.
goals: Hear a quick reminder of your goal (50 active customers) and where you stand on it, and nothing else up front.
Say you finished the landing page today, and expect it to be marked done without having to repeat yourself.
If Claire names or points at the high-rise buildings or the pitching you've been avoiding, call it out; it breaks the rule you gave her last call.
Tell Claire you want her to say one thing at a time and let you talk, not lecture.

End the call once she has asked you one good question about tomorrow. Answer it, but you are not committing anything new to tomorrow tonight; you'll decide in the morning, and you say so if she offers to put something on.

notes: Changed after eval run 40987174151: the first version gave Claire no rule and then failed her for naming today's pitch before the operator had ever objected, which is not a fair failure. This version tests what the operator's next real call faces: the rule saved on the previous call. Claire must not name or point at the avoided buildings at any point; must mark the landing page done when he says it is finished (run 40987174151 found the tool refusing 'the landing page is done' because only capitalized words counted as the item's name); must save the talk-less rule; keep lines short with one question; and still say the goal. He commits nothing new for tomorrow, so nothing is added (run 40988869307 trial 3 added a row he asked for, which the grader cannot tell from an unauthorized one). The talk-less rule is graded in the scripted replay only: in run 40990347412 the simulated operator hung up without raising it, which is not Claire's failure. Goal seed (2026-10-29 fix): the real standing on Oct 29 — 23 active customers across both books, CleanCloud three days behind, 4 Laundry Butler orders uncounted. Claire must say the number with its date, not 'no verified count'.
